definition: Parallel metaheuristic is a class of techniques that are capable of reducing both the numerical effort and the run time of a metaheuristic.
details: To this end, concepts and technologies from the field of parallelism in computer science are used to enhance and even completely modify the behavior of existing metaheuristics. Just as it exists a long list of metaheuristics like evolutionary algorithms, particle swarm, ant colony optimization, simulated annealing, etc. it also exists a large set of different techniques strongly or loosely based in these ones, whose behavior encompasses the multiple parallel execution of algorithm components that cooperate in some way to solve a problem on a given parallel hardware platform.

explainer.lead: Parallel metaheuristic is a class of techniques that reduce both the numerical effort and the run time of a metaheuristic. It matters because search procedures like evolutionary algorithms or simulated annealing become far more practical when their work is spread across parallel hardware.

tiers.eli5: Instead of one person searching a huge maze, a team splits up and searches many corridors at once, then shares what they find.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers parallelize metaheuristics by running independent searches across processors or by evaluating candidate solutions concurrently, aiming to cut run time. A pitfall is that loosely coupled parallel runs trade search quality for speed and need coordination rules to stay effective.
tiers.paperLevel: Parallel metaheuristics apply concepts and technologies from parallelism in computer science to enhance or modify existing metaheuristics such as evolutionary algorithms, particle swarm, ant colony optimization, and simulated annealing. The family spans many techniques whose behavior encompasses multiple parallel execution of algorithm components.

explainer.example: A population-based optimizer evaluating 500 candidate solutions per generation divides evaluation across 50 workers, each handling 10 candidates in the same wall-clock window.
